articles.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s final: Alexander Zverev v Ben Shelton – live
articles.summary: Men’s final updates from 1pm ET/6pm BST Shelton faces date with destiny | Email Ella. As at every US Open final, the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd will be full of famous faces.
body: Shelton had played clean tennis for much of the past two sets, but a few misfires in this game may have swung this match out of his reach. He opens strong with an ace, but then has unforced errors after big 135mph serves on back-to-back points. Zverev breaks and will serve for the championship.

More impressive net work from both players. Zverev sets up 40-0 by catching Shelton at the net and sending a passing two-handed volley into the court behind him. The German holds, and Shelton will have to hold here to stay alive.

Shelton puts his athleticism on display to hold in the fifth game. He pulls out one of his fastest serves of the match, whistling one at 144mph at 40-0. (Not too shabby for three hours in.) He works the baseline at 40-15 and gets a 72mph forehand winner that kisses the line. The American is still alive here, but will need another break like he found at the end of the third set.

articles.title: ‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winner
articles.summary: Officiating body announces it will review the incident. Unhappy Carrick says error was ‘as obvious as it gets’ Pro Ref admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have been awarded, after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in…
body: Haaland’s 60th minute strike for Manchester City at Old Trafford was initially ruled offside before the VAR’s intervention. It came after Josko Gvardiol’s cross hit Patrick Dorgu’s boot, passed Fernández and the United defender Lisandro Martínez, and was finished by the City No 9. VAR decided Fernández was not interfering despite Martínez marking the midfielder.

A Pro Ref statement said: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.
“The on-field decision was offside against Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

“In the same attack, it was established that Fernández did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

articles.title: USA defend Fiba Women’s World Cup title after early scare against France
articles.summary: USA overcame a 14-point France lead in first half. Breanna Stewart scores 22 points; Caitlin Clark gets 12. Defending champions USA fell behind early but stormed back past ⁠France 97-79 on Sunday to win the Women’s World Cup.
body: In a rematch of the 2024 ⁠Olympic final, ⁠the ​American women came out on top once more, earning their fifth consecutive World Cup title ⁠and stretching their impressive unbeaten run at Olympics or World Cups to 20 years.

The perennial red-hot favourites, who had not lost a World Cup match since 2006, the USA were below their best for much of the tournament. They came into Sunday’s game looking vulnerable, having come close to defeats against unheralded Italy and again against Spain in the semi-finals.
No team had come within 20 points of France as they cruised into a maiden World Cup final, and they started strong on Sunday.
The US trailed by two points at half-time to an energetic France side but turned it on when it mattered, outscoring the Europeans 30-12 in the third quarter.

articles.title: Arteta embraces perfect storm to play the victim in game of his own making | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Refereeing is now an impossible job owing to the culture of micro-analysis the Arsenal manager has helped to create. A gentleman is never rude unintentionally, only by design. Nobody really knows who said this first.
body: Every word spoken in front of the board covered in adverts is metered and planned. A manager is never angry, or concerned, or even charming unintentionally. The game is the game, but so are all the other bits spilling out either side of it.

It was hard not to think about this while listening to Mikel Arteta talk about the penalty awarded to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light for a perceived act of grappling on Dan Ballard by Ezri Konsa. This is said with genuine professional respect. As everyone who has ever done a podcast knows – and this is, let’s be clear, everyone – there are lost Amazonian tribes discussing Girls season three in their own dark corner of Spotify – there are moments when you just have to flip the switch, up the energy and turn on full clip‑this‑bit‑up‑please‑Dave sincerity mode.

Arteta did this beautifully in the moment, appearing genuinely struck by what he was saying, radiating wounded integrity, like a disappointed junior headmaster appealing for the return of the school minibus keys.
points: Refereeing is now an impossible job owing to the culture of micro-analysis the Arsenal manager has helped to create.
A gentleman is never rude unintentionally, only by design.
Every word spoken in front of the board covered in adverts is metered and planned.
The game is the game, but so are all the other bits spilling out either side of it.

articles.title: Dominant Kerr wins $150K with GB's first Ultimate title
articles.summary: Josh Kerr ends a sensational season by winning the Ultimate Championship 1500m title as the inaugural edition of athletics' new global event concludes.
body: Josh Kerr ended a sensational season by being crowned Britain's first winner at the Ultimate Championship with a dominant 1500m victory - and earning $150,000 - as the inaugural edition of athletics' new global event concluded in Budapest.

Kerr smashed the 27-year mile world record at the London Diamond League and won Commonwealth Games gold in Glasgow this summer, after beginning an outstanding year by reclaiming the world indoor 3,000m title.

In the shape of his life, Kerr swept past American Yared Nuguse on the back straight in Hungary and would not be denied once he had made his move to the front, taking victory in three minutes 29.35 seconds.
"I am a major championship guy and I will always be that," Kerr, 28, told BBC Sport.

articles.title: Twenty-five years in the waiting - Coventry's nightmare top-flight return
articles.summary: Coventry City's dream return to the Premier League is beginning to unravel after a fourth consecutive defeat - but can Frank Lampard turn it around?
body: Coventry have waited 25 years for a return to the Premier League, but the reality of realising that dream is suddenly starting to look rather miserable.

Their campaign could not have started much worse with four successive defeats all without scoring a goal - the latest a 5-0 thrashing at home to Brighton - highlighting the brutality of the top flight.
The unwanted records are already beginning to pile up for Frank Lampard's side.
It is the club's worst start to a season since 1919-20 when they lost their opening nine matches in what was their first league campaign.

articles.title: How virtual safety car cost Norris win - and should F1 change rules?
articles.summary: Lando Norris says he was "insanely unlucky" to lose what seemed like a certain win in the Spanish Grand Prix because of the timing of a virtual safety car.
body: McLaren's Norris was leading comfortably when the VSC was called, seconds after he had passed the pit lane entry.
That allowed Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen to pit under the VSC, saving time, while the caution period ended before Norris could make it around to the pits again.
Of the VSC, Norris said: "It is a rule that should not define a whole race."
"I was the only one on the whole grid that didn't get the chance to do the pit stop," he said. "That's just unfortunate.

articles.title: Awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd an error, admits refereeing body
articles.summary: Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.
body: In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.
The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Despite not touching the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to impact the defending of Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez before Haaland's back-post finish, which by the laws of the game should have led to the goal remaining disallowed.

articles.title: 'We gotta keep proving it.' What the Bengals defense show in Week 1 win
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe said the team wanted to use Week 1 to declare its intent to the rest of the NFL and to gain a better understanding of the retooled defense's capabilities. "We came into this game saying we’ve got to make a statement," Mafe said.
body: Week 1 always comes with some limitations, especially for defenses that likely haven't done any real tackling since the end of last season. But by the end of the Bengals' Sept. 13 opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium, it was hard to imagine AFC North rivals and others wouldn't have noticed Cincinnati's defensive output.
The Bengals won their opener 33-27, and the defense produced like the team's personnel decision-makers would have hoped after an offseason personnel overhaul.

Defensive coordinator Al Golden's unit scored a touchdown − a 27-yard fumble was recovered and returned by Demetrius Knight Jr. in the first quarter − and held Tampa Bay 's offense to 20 points. The Buccaneers' defense provided a pick-6 touchdown to make the game tighter in the second half.
Dexter Lawrence Jr., the organization's prized offseason trade acquisition, didn't register a tackle. Plenty of others, Bengals both new and veteran, contributed big days statistically.

body: Nordqvist's side completed a 15-13 victory over Team USA after prevailing in Sunday's singles in the Netherlands.
The scores were tied at 8-8 following the opening two days, but USA captain Angela Stanford felt her side had been at a disadvantage throughout the tournament due to the slowness of the greens.
Stanford said at her post-tournament press conference: "Europe played well. I don't think we played bad. I think we just didn't make enough putts.
"And if you listen to everything I've ever said, Europeans always putt better. I don't know why. I still don't know why. I mean, I have a good idea, but I'm not going to say it right now.

articles.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
articles.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.
However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.
